input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 2.1 imposes a multi-year (three-year) USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — walk-away territory under MINCOMMIT, and it fails every fallback element (no 12-month limit, no 30-day reduction right, no true-up). It also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment. We therefore target the preferred position with the shortest edit: replace the offending commitment sentence with an express no-minimum-purchase-or-volume statement. The second preferred element is already met by Section 7.1, which obliges Customer to pay only the Fees stated in each Order Form (with usage-based unit pricing where an Order Form so provides), so no further language is added. No other clause imposes volume caps or shortfall penalties on Customer (the Section 22.2/22.3 "shortfall" references concern Vendor underpayment audits).

ops.oldText: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay expressly stripped of reduction or termination rights, so we have replaced Section 2.1 with a statement that Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment, consistent with Section 12.3 and leaving Section 7.1 to govern payment for Fees actually ordered. If a commitment is commercially essential, we could discuss one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
proposal.summary: Replace the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay in Section 2.1 with an express no-minimum-commitment statement.
